title: Whole Grain Pasta with Tomato Sauce and Vegetables

content.title: About
content.content: Whole grain pasta with a tomato‑based sauce and added vegetables is a dish made from whole‑grain pasta topped with a sauce made from tomatoes and mixed with fresh vegetables such as bell pepper, zucchini, and carrot. Served at restaurant (3643), it combines the nutritional benefits of whole grains, lycopene from tomatoes, and vitamins from the vegetables.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole grain pasta contains more fiber and micronutrients than traditional white pasta.
Tomato sauce is rich in lycopene, an antioxidant that becomes more bioavailable after cooking.
Vegetables retain a portion of their vitamins and minerals, especially when lightly sautéed rather than overcooked.
The dish is often featured in restaurants focused on healthy eating as part of a balanced menu.
The combination of whole grain and vegetables helps maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Whole grain pasta provides dietary fiber that supports healthy digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Antioxidant effect
items.content: Lycopene from tomatoes helps protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: The added vegetables contribute vitamin C, vitamin A, potassium, and folate, supporting immunity and skin health.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Whole grain pasta has a lower GI than refined pasta, which is beneficial for blood‑sugar control.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Fiber and antioxidants aid in lowering LDL cholesterol levels.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Whole grain pasta contains gluten, which can trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Tomato sauce can be salty; individuals monitoring sodium intake should check the amount.

items.title: Tomato acidity
items.content: For some people, tomato‑based sauce may cause heartburn or stomach irritation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the pasta hot, mixing the sauce and vegetables together. Optional additions include a drizzle of olive oil, grated Parmesan, or fresh herbs. The dish is eaten with a fork or spoon.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Keep dry whole grain pasta in a cool, dry place in a sealed package.
